headline: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) has denied social media claims that U.S. personnel were injured in recent Iranian attacks and medically evacuated, calling them “FALSE.” The claims followed a U.S. Air Force C-17A 'Globemaster III' departing Ramstein Air Base, Germany, using the call sign “BNDGE01,” which is associated with aeromedical evacuation flights. According to flight data, the aircraft was headed to Baghdad International Airport, Iraq. The U.S. military completed its withdrawal of troops from Iraq on September 30th, however a small number of troops remain to secure the green zone and embassy. There have been no recently reported attacks on U.S. personnel or assets in Iraq, indicating that the medical evacuation flight is related to a non-combat illness or injury.

headline: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has published updated guidance from the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) on the U.S. naval blockade of Iran. The guidance states that any ship receiving cargo through a ship-to-ship transfer from a vessel loaded in Iranian waters may be considered to be evading the blockade, “even if it has not entered Iranian ports or the Iranian coastline.” Ships that do not comply with orders from U.S. forces enforcing the blockade are subject to enforcement measures, including the use of force, according to the notice.
